checklist.title: Verify Bloom Filter Bit Index Invariant: Is bit_to_set always constrained to [0, 2047] by the 11-bit mask (AND 0x07FF)?

reachability.notes: If the 0x07FF mask is incorrectly implemented (e.g., 0x0FFF for 12 bits), bit_to_set could exceed 2047, causing byte_index to exceed 255.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate all implementations of add_to_bloom function across client codebases. 2. Verify the bitmask constant is exactly 0x07FF (2047 in decimal, 11 bits). 3. Check for any alternative mask values (e.g., 0x0FFF for 12 bits, 0x00FF for 8 bits) that would violate the invariant. 4. Compute the maximum possible byte_index when bit_to_set = 2047 (should be 255, i.e., 2047 / 8 = 255). 5. Attempt to craft transactions with log topics that, when hashed, produce values where incorrect masking would cause byte_index > 255. 6. Compare bloom filter outputs across different client implementations for the same transaction logs to detect divergence. 7. Verify no out-of-bounds memory access occurs when bit_to_set approaches boundary values.

falsification_approach.property_to_violate: bit_to_set must always be in [0, 2047] after masking
attack_vectors: Missing mask application in code path
Integer type mismatch causing truncation issues
falsification_approach.expected_consequence: byte_index exceeds 255, causing out-of-bounds array access or consensus-critical bloom filter divergence

checklist.consensus_impact: Receipt root divergence leading to chain split between clients with correct vs incorrect mask implementation
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0030, Invariant: SG-001-bloom/INV-002, Assumption: asm-006, Threat: stride-007. Primary element: SG-001-bloom. This is an internal logic invariant that must hold to prevent consensus failures.
